function: p. 5-7: Hierarchical DRL: RP-agent allocates RISs to operators; OP-agents jointly learn BS beamforming, RIS phase shifts and user association to maximize the sum rate.
system: p. 3-4, 10: 2 operators, each 2 BSs (10 antennas) and 5 single-antenna users; 4 passive frequency-selective 20-element RISs; Rician channels; carrier frequency not stated.
method: p. 5-9: Hierarchical PPO actor-critic RL on an SMDP: RP-agent (LSTM+FC) allocates RISs; OP-agents (FC, Beta policy) choose beamforming, phase shifts, association; S-HPPO variant for large RIS counts.
data_channel: p. 4, 10: Own simulator: Rician fading (kappa=10), path-loss exponents 2.5/2.8/3.5, BSs on 150 m semicircle, users in 5-7 m annulus; RL agents interact with this environment.
test_conditions: p. 10-13: Training and evaluation inside each simulated setting; RIS size, BSs, OPs, Rician factor, power and RIS count vary between curves; no unseen-setting test stated.
baselines: p. 11-13: Non-learned RP-level rules: auction [21], distance, random, greedy (with PPO at OPs); no-RIS PPO; learned SAC, DDPG at OPs and DDQN at RP; centralized PPO; 1D-HPPO.
metrics: p. 10-13: Sum-rate (bps/Hz) curves over episodes, versus transmit power, RIS elements and RIS count; update and inference runtime (Fig. 16).
complexity: p. 10, 13: Complexity orders in layer widths for inference and update (Table I, Sec. IV-D); measured update and inference runtime of S-HPPO versus HPPO (Fig. 16).
q1_support: p. 4: "All sub-channels follow Rician fading"; p. 10: "The pass-loss exponents for the BS-RIS, RIS-user, and BS-user channels are 2.5, 2.8, and 3.5, respectively" (own simulator; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is used)
q2_support: p. 10: "instantaneous sum-rates for each episode are depicted with transparent lines, while the smoothed average rate over a 100-episode window is shown with solid lines"; p. 11: "Fig. 6 shows the effect of varying RIS elements" (one convergence curve per setting; no policy trained in one setting is tested in another)
q3_support: p. 12: "the RP-agent implements various RIS allocation benchmarks" (non-learned auction [21], distance, random, greedy); p. 11: "we implement soft actor-critic (SAC) and deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithms" (sum-rate, Figs. 10-14)
q4_support: p. 10: "Table I compares the computational complexity of the inference phase for S-HPPO and HPPO"; p. 13: "we compare the runtime of S-HPPO and HPPO"
q5_support: p. 10: "BSs are randomly distributed along a semicircular region with a radius of 150m" (own simulated environment; no code or data link and no public dataset anywhere in the paper)
notes: RIS allocation by the RP-agent and user association are above the physical layer, but the OP-agents also learn BS beamforming and RIS phase shifts jointly with them (p. 1, p. 7), so the work passes above_phy; area 3. q1: only a custom Rician simulator with path-loss exponents (p. 4, p. 10). q3: the non-learned baselines are RP-level allocation rules with PPO kept at the OPs, and the learned baselines are SAC, DDPG and DDQN inside the same hierarchical framework (Fig. 10, p. 11); there is no non-learned beamforming or phase-shift baseline at the OP level, so the reviewer should confirm. q2: every curve is a convergence run for one setting. The carrier frequency is not given in the text.
